rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tadhkira means reminder or admonition, referring either to the Qur’an or to other exhortations.
rows.anchor: عن التذكير وهو العظة ، يريد : القرآن أو غيره من المواعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿriḍīn is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, as in the expression ‘what is the matter with you standing?’
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال ، كقولك : مالك قائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, mustanfira describes wild asses intensely fleeing, as if they themselves seek and urge flight.
rows.anchor: الشديدة النفار كأنها تطلب النفار من نفوسها في جمعها له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa reading means ‘made to flee’ or ‘frightened into flight.’
rows.anchor: وهي المنفرة المحمولة على النفار : والقسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qaswara can mean a band of archers who hunt wild asses.
rows.anchor: جماعة الرماة الذين يتصيدونها . وقيل : الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes al-qaswara to mean a lion; the word is on the faʿūla pattern from qasr, overpowering and subduing.
rows.anchor: يقال : ليوث قساور وهي فعولة من القسر : وهو القهر والغلبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains al-qaswara as the clamor and voices of people.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ركز الناس وأصواتهم . وعن عكرمة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima explains al-qaswara as the darkness of night.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة : ظلمة الليل ، شبههم في إعراضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their avoidance of Qur’an and admonition is likened to startled wild asses bolting; the comparison plainly censures their foolishness and lack of sense, like the donkey carrying books.
rows.anchor: شبههم في إعراضهم عن القرآن واستماع الذكر والموعظة وشرادهم عنه ، بحمر جدت في نفارها مما أفزعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vivid simile draws on the especially swift stampede of wild asses when startled, a standard Arab comparison for camels’ speed and flight from hunters at water.
rows.anchor: ولا ترى مثل نفار حمير الوحش واطرادها في العدو إذا رأبها رائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scattered sheets can be open papers or letters like those people exchange, or heavenly books newly written and brought by angels, still fresh and unfolded.
rows.anchor: قراطيس تنشر وقرأ كالكتب التي يتكاتب بها أو كتبا كتبت في السماء ونزلت بها الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demanded that each person receive a heavenly document addressed by God by name and commanding him to follow the Messenger; the same demand appears elsewhere.
rows.anchor: لن نتبعك حتى تأتي كل واحد منا بكتب من السماء عنوانها من رب العالمين إلى فلان بن فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report of their demand is that every man wake to find a sheet declaring his innocence and safety from the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قالوا إن كان محمد صادقا فليصبح عند رأس كل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءته وأمنه من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also invoked a claim about Israelites waking to find their sin and expiation written above them; al-Zamakhsharī says this is remote from the phrase unless it means publicly exposed writings.
rows.anchor: بلغنا أن الرجل من بني إسرائيل كان يصبح مكتوبا على رأسه ذنبه وكفارته

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads both words with light consonants; anshara and nashara have the same sense, like anzala and nazzala.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير : ( صحفا منشرة ) بتخفيفهما ، على أن أنشر الصحف ونشرها : واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects their wish for extraordinary documents and rebukes them for demanding signs.
rows.anchor: ردعهم بقوله { كلا } عن تلك الإرادة ، وزجرهم عن اقتراح الآيات ، ثم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their real reason for turning away from the reminder is that they do not fear the Hereafter, not that the requested sheets were withheld.
rows.anchor: فلذلك أعرضوا عن التذكرة لا لامتناع إيتاء الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a powerful and sufficient reminder, which itself rebukes their rejection of admonition.
rows.anchor: ثم ردعهم عن إعراضهم عن التذكرة وقال : { إنه تذكرة } يعني تذكرة بليغة كافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever chooses may remember the reminder, retain it, and make it his concern; its benefit returns to him.
rows.anchor: أن يذكره ولا ينساه ويجعله عينه فعل ، فإن نفع ذلك راجع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in ‘it is a reminder’ and ‘remember it’ refer to al-tadhkira in 74:49; masculine forms reflect its sense as dhikr or Qur’an.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { إنه } و { ذكره } للتذكرة في قوله { فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين } ( المدثر : 49 ) وإنما ذكر لأنها في معنى الذكر أو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remember only if God compels them to remember, since their hearts are sealed and they will not believe by choice.
rows.anchor: يعني : إلا أن يقسرهم على الذكر ويلجئهم إليه . لأنهم مطبوع على قلوبهم . معلوم أنهم لا يؤمنون اختيارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rightly deserves His servants’ fear and obedience, and is worthy to forgive them when they believe and obey.
rows.anchor: هو حقيق بأن يتقيه عباده ، ويخافوا عقابه ، فيؤمنوا ويطيعوا ، وحقيق بأن يغفر لهم إذا آمنوا وأطاعوا

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet’s explanation: God deserves to be feared and forgives whoever fears Him.
rows.anchor: هو أهل أن يتقي ، وأهل أن يغفر لمن اتقاه

words: وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadhkurūn is read with yāʾ or tāʾ, and with light or doubled dhāl.
rows.anchor:
بالياء والتاء مخففا ومشددا .
عن رسول الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises ten good deeds for each person in Mecca who believed in Muhammad or disbelieved in him to whoever recites al-Muddaththir; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة المدثر أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد من صدق بمحمد وكذب به بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qiyāma is Meccan, has forty verses, and was revealed after al-Qāriʿa.
rows.anchor: مكية ، وآياتها 40 ( نزلت بعد القارعة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes preferring worldly life to the Hereafter and calls people to notice death, when present life ends and everlasting afterlife begins.
rows.anchor: ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة ، كأنه قيل : ارتدعوا عن ذلك ، وتنبهوا على ما بين أيديكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed subject of ‘reaches’ is the soul; the surrounding discourse makes it clear, just as Arabic may say ‘it rained’ without naming the sky.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { بلغت } للنفس وإن لم يجر لها ذكر ، لأن الكلام الذي وقعت فيه يدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥātim’s verse illustrates the soul’s death rattle and constricted chest; the Arabs likewise say ‘I sent’ meaning that rain came, without mentioning the sky.
rows.anchor: كما قال حاتم : أماوي ما يغني الثراء عن الفتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tarāqī are the bones on either side enclosing the hollow at the base of the neck.
rows.anchor: { التراقي } العظام المكتنفة لثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال . ذكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse evokes death’s severity as the soul reaches the collarbones and its departure nears, the first stage of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم صعوبة الموت الذي هو أول مراحل الآخرة حين تبلغ الروح التراقي ودنا زهوقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation has those present around the dying person asking who among them can perform ruqya for his affliction.
rows.anchor: وقال حاضرة واصاحبها وهو المحتضر بعضهم لبعض { من راق } أيكم يرقيه مما به ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes this the speech of the death angels asking which group will take the soul up, the angels of mercy or punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو كلام ملائكة الموت : أيكم يرقى بروحه ؟ ملائكة الرحمة أم ملائكة العذاب ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person realizes that what has befallen him means separation from the world he loved.
rows.anchor: { وظن } المحتضر { أنه الفراق } أن هذا الذي نزل به هو فراق الدنيا المحبوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legs twist around one another during the convulsions of death.
rows.anchor: { والتفت } ساقه بساقه والتوت عليها عند علز الموت . وعن قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the legs have died and can no longer carry the person who once traveled on them.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : ماتت رجلاه فلا تحملانه ، وقد كان عليهما جوالا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes ‘leg’ as hardship: the hardship of leaving this world meets the hardship of the Hereafter’s arrival.
rows.anchor: وقيل : شدة فراق الدنيا بشدة إقبال الآخرة ، على أن الساق في الشدة .

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says the two legs are the person’s legs as they are wrapped in his shroud.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب : هما ساقاه حين تلفان في أكفانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-masāq is being driven to God and His judgment.
rows.anchor: { المساق } أي يساق إلى الله وإلى حكمه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He created and determined the human being, then proportioned him perfectly.
rows.anchor: فخلق } فقدر { فسوى } فعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-zawjayn means the two kinds, male and female.
rows.anchor: { منه } من الإنسان { الزوجين } الصنفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who originated this creation is surely able to restore it.
rows.anchor: { أليس ذلك } الذي أنشأ هذا الإنشاء { بقادر } على الإعادة .

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet would answer this verse when reciting it with ‘Glory be to You, yes indeed.’
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأها قال ( سبحانك بلى ) .

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises that he and Gabriel will testify on Resurrection Day that the reciter believed in it; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة القيامة شهدت له أنا وجبريل يوم القيامة أنه كان مؤمنا بيوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Insān is described as Medinan, with thirty-one verses, revealed after al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: مدنية ، ورياتها 31 ( نزلت بعد الرحمن

words: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَنزِيلًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the pronoun after making it the subject doubles emphasis on God’s exclusive role as revealer and assures the Prophet that the staged revelation follows wisdom.
rows.anchor: تكرير الضمير بعد إيقاعه إسما لان : تأكيد على تأكيد لمعنى اختصاص الله بالتنزيل

words: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَنزِيلًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God sent the Qur’an down to the Prophet in stages; as the wise author of every act, He revealed patience and forbearance now and will later command fighting and retribution.
rows.anchor: ما نزل عليك القرآن تنزيلا مفرقا منجما إلا أنا لا غيري ، وقد عرفتني حكيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must patiently accept his Lord’s wise decree, including the delay of victory over his Meccan enemies for wise interests.
rows.anchor: { فاصبر لحكم ربك } الصادر عن الحكمة وتعليقه الأمور بالمصالح ، وتأخيره نصرتك على أعدائك من أهل مكة

words: وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite intense hostility and abuse, the Meccan opponents invited the Prophet to abandon his mission, offering wealth and marriage to their most eminent daughters.
rows.anchor: وكانوا مع إفراطهم في العداوة والإيذاء له ولمن معه يدعونه إلى أن يرجع عن أمره ويبذلون له أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition covers helping someone who invites the Prophet to a sinful act or to disbelief, but not an invitation to something that is neither sin nor disbelief.
rows.anchor: نهى أن يساعدهم على الاثنين دون الثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported identification makes the sinner ʿUtba and the unbeliever al-Walīd; ʿUtba was persistently sinful, while al-Walīd was exceptionally stubborn in disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الآثم عتبة ؛ والكفور : الوليد ؛ لأن عتبة كان ركابا للمآثم ، متعاطيا لأنهواع الفسوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here aw means ‘either one’; forbidding obedience to either rules out obeying both, just as forbidding even ‘uff’ to parents rules out striking them a fortiori.
rows.anchor: كما إذا نهى أن يقولا لأبويه : أف ، علم أنه منهى عن ضربهما على طريق الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the Lord morning and evening means maintaining the dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: { واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا } ودم على صلاة الفجر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Prostrate to Him at night’ can mean pray during part of the night, or refer to the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers.
rows.anchor: { ومن اليل فاسجد له } وبعض الليل فصل له . أو يعني صلاة المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min marks a portion of the night, as it can mark a portion of an object in ‘He forgives you some of your sins.’
rows.anchor: وأدخل ( من ) على الظرف للتبعيض ، كما دخل على المفعول في قوله : { يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to worship during a long portion of the night, construed as two-thirds, one-half, or one-third of it.
rows.anchor: { وسبحه ليلا طويلا } وتهجد له هزيعا طويلا من الليل : ثلثيه ، أو نصفه ، أو ثلثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses deniers of resurrection: are you harder to create than the heaven?
rows.anchor: الخطاب لمنكرى ا لبعث ، يعني { أءنتم } أصعب { خلقا } وإنشاء { أم السمآء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God built the heaven by raising its height to a vast expanse, described as a journey of five hundred years upward.
rows.anchor: { رفع سمكها } أي جعل مقدار ذهابها في سمت العلو مديدا رفيعا مسيرة خمسمائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says He made the heaven even and smooth, with no disparity or fissures; another says He completed and set it right as needed.
rows.anchor: { فسواها } فعدلها مستوية ملساء ، ليس فيها تفاوت ولا فطور . أو فتممها بما علم أنها تتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aghtasha is a causative form, ‘God made it dark,’ parallel to ẓalama/aẓlamahu; the night itself may also be said to have become dark.
rows.anchor: غطش الليل وأغطشه الله ، كقولك : ظلم وأظلمه . ويقال أيضا : أغطش الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven’s ḍuḥā is the sun’s light; the cited verse likewise means its light, and ḍuḥā is when the sun rises and prevails.
rows.anchor: { وأخرج ضحاها } وأبرز ضوء شمسها ، يدل عليه قوله تعالى : { والشمس وضحاها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and sun are attributed to heaven because night is its shadow and the sun is the piercing lamp in its atmosphere.
rows.anchor: وأضيف الليل والشمس إلى السماء ، لأن الليل ظلها والشمس هي السراج المثقب في جوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its water means springs that gush forth.
rows.anchor: { ماءها } عيونها المتفجرة بالماء { ومرعاها } ورعيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marʿāhā means its grazing or pasture, originally the place where grazing occurs.
rows.anchor: { ومرعاها } ورعيها ، وهو في الأصل موضع الرعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-arḍ and al-jibāl are accusative under omitted verbs, ‘He spread’ and ‘He fixed’; al-Ḥasan reads both nominative as subjects.
rows.anchor: ونصب الأرض والجبال بإضمار ( دحا ) و ( أرسى ) وهو الإضمار على شريطة التفسير . وقرأهما الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two explanations account for the lack of a conjunction before ‘He brought forth’: it explains what spreading earth entails, or it is a circumstantial clause with an implied qad.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون معنى { دحاها } بسطها ومهدها للسكنى ، ثم فسر التمهيد بما لا بد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pasture includes what people and animals eat; grazing is metaphorically used for people as in ‘roam and play,’ and one reading uses nartaʿu.
rows.anchor: وأراد بمرعاها : ما يأكل الناس والأنعام . واستعير الرعي للإنسان كما استعير الرتع في قوله : { نخوض ونلعب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning water and pasture signals all earthly benefits and enjoyments, even salt, since salt comes from water.
rows.anchor: دل الله سبحانه بذكر الماء والمرعى على عامة ما يرتفق به ويتمتع مما يخرج من الأرض حتى الملح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepared these provisions for the enjoyment of people and their livestock.
rows.anchor: { متاعا لكم } فعل ذلك تمتيعا لكم { ولانعامكم } لأن منفعة ذلك التمهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion report says Ibn Umm Maktūm approached while the Prophet urged Quraysh leaders to accept Islam; the blind man repeatedly asked for teaching, and the Prophet frowned and turned away while occupied with them.
rows.anchor: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ابن أم مكتوم وأم مكتوم أم أبيه ، واسمه عبد الله بن شريح ابن مالك بن ربيعة الفهري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report identifies Ibn Umm Maktūm as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shurayḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihrī; Umm Maktūm was his mother’s name.
rows.anchor: وعنده صناديد قريش : عتبة وشيبة ابنا ربيعة ، وأبو جهل بن هشام . والعباس بن عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the revelation, the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktūm, welcomed him as the one for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and twice appointed him over Medina.
rows.anchor: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكرمه ويقول إذا رآه : مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.
rows.anchor: وقال أنس : رأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع وله راية سوداء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A doubled sīn reading intensifies the meaning of ‘he frowned.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( عبس ) بالتشديد للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Depending on the grammatical analysis, an jāʾahu is governed by tawallā or by ʿabasa.
rows.anchor: أن جآءه } منصوب بتولى ، أو بعبس ، على اختلاف المذهبين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has two hamzas with an alif between them; pausing after ‘he frowned and turned away’ then beginning ‘because the blind man came?’ makes it an explicit rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( أن جاءه ) بهمزتين وبألف بينهما ، ووقف على { عبس وتولى } ثم ابتديء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that afterward the Prophet never again frowned at a poor person or turned his attention toward a rich one.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه ما عبس بعدها في وجه فقير قط ، ولا تصدى لغني .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reporting the lapse first and then directly addressing the Prophet heightens the censure, like publicly complaining about a wrong before confronting its perpetrator.
rows.anchor: وفي الإخبار عما فرط منه ، ثم الإقبال عليه بالخطاب : دليل على زيادة الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the blind man underscores the reproach: if his blindness seemed to warrant turning away, it should instead have inspired greater compassion, welcome, and closeness.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر الأعمى نحو من ذلك ، كأنه يقول : قد استحق عنده العبوس والإعراض لأنه أعمى

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī is reported to have said that poor people were the leaders in his gatherings, reflecting the good etiquette people learned from this verse.
rows.anchor: فقد روي عن سفيان الثوري رحمه الله أن الفقراء كانوا في مجلسه أمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: what could make you know the blind man’s true state?
rows.anchor: { وما يدريك } وأي شيء يجعلك داريا بحال هذا الأعمى ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the pronoun as the blind man: he may purify himself by learning religious law and shedding sin, or take admonition that helps him obey; the Prophet could not know what might follow.
rows.anchor: أي يتطهر بما يتلقن من الشرائع من بعض أوضار الإثم ( { أو يذكر } أو يتعظ { فتنفعه } ذكراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the pronoun as the unbeliever: the Prophet hoped Islam and the reminder would bring him toward truth, though he could not know that this would happen.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير في { لعله } للكافر . يعني أنك طمعت في أن يتزكى بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatanfaʿahu is read in the indicative, coordinated with yadhdhakkaru, or in the subjunctive as a response to laʿalla; the latter syntax is paralleled elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( فتنفعه ) ، بالرفع عطفا على يذكر . وبالنصب جوابا للعل ، كقوله : { فأطلع إلى إلاه موسى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣaddā means to present oneself by turning toward someone; muṣādā means opposition.
rows.anchor: { تصدى } تتعرض بالإقبال عليه ، والمصاداة ، المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A doubled reading assimilates tāʾ into ṣād; Abū Jaʿfar reads with ḍamma on tāʾ, meaning ‘you present yourself.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( تصدى ) بالتشديد ، بإدغام التاء في الصاد . وقرأ أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was urged by eagerness to win the Quraysh leaders; he was not responsible if they failed to become Muslims.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : يدعوك داع إلى التصدي له : من الحرص والتهالك على إسلامه ، وليس عليك بأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasʿā means that the poor man hastens in seeking good.
rows.anchor: { يسعى } يسرع في طلب الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may fear God, fear the unbelievers and their harm as he comes to the Prophet, or fear stumbling because he has no guide.
rows.anchor: { وهو يخشى } الله أو يخشى الكفار ، وأذاهم في إتيانك . وقيل : جاء وليس معه قائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talāhā means to be occupied or distracted from someone; the source also notes related forms from the root lahā.
rows.anchor: { تلهى } تتشاغل ، من لهى عنه . والتهى . وتلهى .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif reads tatallahā, while Abū Jaʿfar reads talhā, meaning the chiefs’ affairs distract you.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف : ( تتلهى ) ، وقرأ أبو جعفر ( تلهى ) أي : يلهيك شأن الصناديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing singles out the Prophet for reproach: someone of his stature should not turn toward the rich and neglect the poor.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : قوله : { فأنت له تصدى } ، ( فأنت عنه تلهى ) كأن فيه اختصاصا قلت : نعم ، ومعناه : إنكار التصدي والتلهي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After enumerating blessings in the human being, the passage turns to blessings needed for life and calls people to consider how God arranged their food.
rows.anchor: ولما عدد النعم في نفسه : أتبعه ذكر النعم فيما يحتاج إليه ، فقال : { فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food means the sustenance by which people live; ‘We poured water’ refers to rain.
rows.anchor: إلى مطعمه الذي يعيش به كيف دبرنا أمره ( أنا صببنا الماء ) يعني الغيث .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anā is read with kasra as a new sentence or with fatḥa as an apposition to ‘food’; al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī reads annā with imāla, ‘how We poured.’
rows.anchor: قرىء بالكسر على الاستئناف ، وبالفتح على البدل من الطعام ، وقرأ الحسين بن علي رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s splitting can mean the opening made by plants, or furrows cut by ox-drawn plows; the action is ascribed to God as its ultimate cause.
rows.anchor: وشققنا : من شق الأرض بالنبات ويجوز أن يكون من شقها بالكراب على البقر ؛ وأسند الشك إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥabb includes all harvested grains, such as wheat and barley.
rows.anchor: والحب : كل ما حصد من نحو الحنطة والشعير وغيرهما .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaḍb is fresh fodder; maqḍab is its land, named from qaḍaba, ‘to cut,’ because it is cut repeatedly.
rows.anchor: والقضب : الرطبة والمقضاب : أرضه ، سمي بمصدر قضبه إذا قطعه ؛ لأنه يقضب مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghulban can describe each garden as dense, abundant in trees, and large, or describe its trees as thick and massive; the adjective is borrowed from thick necks.
rows.anchor: { وحدائق غلبا } يحتمل أن يجعل كل حديقة غلباء ، فيريد تكاثفها وكثرة أشجارها وعظمها

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: A line by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib uses ghulb to describe thick necks, illustrating the word’s original sense.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن معد يكرب : يمشي بها غلب الرقاب كأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-abb is pasture, named from a-bba, to set out for and seek it; al-abb and al-umm are paired terms.
rows.anchor: والأب : المرعى ، لأنه يؤب أي يؤم وينتجع . والأب والأم أخوان

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: A cited line about Qays and Najd uses al-abb alongside al-makraʿ as a pasture term.
rows.anchor: قال : جذمنا قيس ونجد دارنا … ولنا الأب به والمكرع

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: When asked about al-abb, Abū Bakr refused to speculate about God’s Book without knowledge, asking what sky would shelter him and what earth would support him if he did.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه سئل عن الأب فقال

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar asked what al-abb meant, called pursuing the answer needless effort, and advised following what is clear in the Book and leaving what is not.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه : أنه قرأ هذه الآية فقال : كل هذا قد عرفنا ، فما الأب ؟ ثم رفض عصا كانت بيده وقال : هذا لعمر الله التكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports do not prohibit investigating difficult Qur’anic meanings; they criticize neglecting actionable gratitude to chase a detail with no practical use.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : فهذا يشبه النهي عن تتبع معاني القرآن والبحث عن مشكلاته . قلت : لم يذهب إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage thanks God for provisions; context makes clear that al-abb is a plant God provides for people or livestock, so general understanding suffices until its exact botanical referent becomes clear.
rows.anchor: فأراد أن الآية مسوقة في الامتنان علي الإنسان بمطعمه واستدعاء شكره ، وقد علم من فحوى الآية أن الأب بعض ما أنبته الله للإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesson for interpreting similarly difficult passages is to follow this same practice: avoid distraction by obscure details when their exact identification is not needed.
rows.anchor: ثم وصى الناس بأن يجروا على هذا السنن فيما أشبه ذلك من مشكلات القرآن
